draft.title: Debt and credit
card: Debt is money you owe. You can borrow with a credit card, a loan or buy now pay later (BNPL), which lets you take an item home and pay for it in parts.
Borrowing can cost more than paying upfront. Interest is a charge for borrowing money, and some products also add fees.
For example, a $500 phone bought on credit may end up costing $560 once interest and fees are added.
A credit record is a history of how you repay what you borrow. Missed payments can harm it and make future borrowing harder.
draft.remember: Borrowing usually costs more than paying upfront, and missed payments can harm your credit record.

a.q: Why can buying a $300 jacket on credit cost more than paying $300 upfront?
opts: Interest and fees are added to the price
The shop raises the price of the jacket
Credit records add a charge each year
Only the first payment includes the $300
a.why: Borrowing can add interest and fees on top of the price, so the total paid can be above $300. A credit record tracks repayments. It is not a charge.
a.clue: Think about what lenders add when you borrow.

b.q: Sam buys a $200 skateboard using BNPL but misses two payments. What is the most likely result?
opts: Late fees may be added and his credit record may be harmed
The debt is cancelled because the board is already his
He pays less because the first payment was on time
His credit record improves because he used BNPL
b.why: Missed payments can lead to late fees and can harm a credit record. Paying in parts does not remove the debt, and missing payments does not make it cheaper.
b.clue: What can happen when payments are missed?

a.best: Interest and fees are added to the price

b.best: Late fees may be added and his credit record may be harmed

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with a hedge ('may'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The question and why rely on 'late fees', but the card mentions only that some products add fees, not fees for missed payments. Students must infer late fees from outside the card.
The remember line says borrowing 'usually' costs more, which is stronger than the card's 'can cost more'.
